title: Functions: 15 distinct forms
outcome: Build callable components with clear parameters, returns, and ownership.

steps.title: 1. Input and return
steps.text: A function accepts arguments and returns a value. In these drills, define exactly the function name/signature in the contract. The checker calls it with several inputs.

steps.title: 2. Call signatures
steps.text: Positional and keyword arguments provide different calling forms. Defaults apply only when an argument is omitted. A * in a signature makes later parameters keyword-only; / makes earlier parameters positional-only.

steps.title: 3. Return information, not just text
steps.text: Returning a structured result makes logic reusable. Printing is a separate interface decision. Multiple return values are usually a tuple.

steps.title: 4. Treat functions as values
steps.text: A callback is a function supplied to another function. Dependency injection passes a collector into analysis so it can be replaced during tests.
steps.code:
def collect_names(fetch):
    return [row["name"] for row in fetch()]

steps.title: 5. Verify repeated calls
steps.text: Mutable defaults are created once. Use None then allocate inside the function. Test repeated calls and supplied containers to expose accidental shared state.

Compare the implementation with case 03-small. Trace the supplied inputs and the exact return/output type before changing the code.
